strategy.summary: Timedelta divided (/ or //) by a float32/float64 numpy ndarray saturates to int64 max instead of raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta when the quotient leaves the int64 range; the fix adds a float64 overflow check (threshold 2**63) in the scalar path, exempting zero and nan divisors which must still yield NaT. The developer's test test_td_div_float_ndarray_overflow should fail on buggy ebd40365c94b and pass on the fixed revision after a compiled Cython build.

system_packages: a C compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython are documented in README.md but carry no version constraint in the evidence; no era ceiling was stated, so versions are unpinned and chosen as current releases compatible with the checked-out source tree
Python version not stated by evidence; use the interpreter the repository's current pyproject requires

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest pandas/tests/scalar/timedelta/test_arithmetic.py -k 'test_td_div_float_ndarray_overflow or test_td_div_ndarray_zero_or_nan_still_nat or test_td_div_ndarray_in_bounds' -v
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy ebd40365c94b, test_td_div_float_ndarray_overflow fails for all parametrizations (unit in s,ms,us,ns; dtype in f8,f4) because td / other and td // other return a saturated timedelta64 array instead of raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta, so pytest.raises reports 'DID NOT RAISE'. On the fixed revision the same test passes, with both operations raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta matching 'Overflow in timedelta division'. The companion zero/nan and in-bounds tests should pass on both revisions, acting as guards against over-broad fixes.
strategy.numerical_probe: Timedelta(4, 'ns') / np.array([1e-300]) on buggy returns array([9223372036854775807]) dtype m8[ns]; on fixed it raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta
risks: The overflow path needs a float ndarray divisor; the bug is platform-independent in pure Python arithmetic, but the saturation value depends on numpy's float-to-int64 cast behaviour, which can differ on some platforms, so the buggy-revision failure text may vary even though the DID NOT RAISE failure should hold.

Zero float divisor triggers numpy divide-by-zero RuntimeWarning; if pytest is configured with filterwarnings=error the zero/nan test may fail for reasons unrelated to the fix, so run with the project's default warning config.

Test references GH#66552 while the PR is #66670; the test file also includes test_td_mul_lands_on_nat_sentinel and test_td_add_sub_lands_on_nat_sentinel from the same branch, which are not part of this bug and are not required to transition.

The reproduction requires a compiled Cython build of the checked-out revision; an editable install that is stale against the buggy or fixed Cython source would invalidate the transition, so rebuild after switching revisions.

Build was not verified on a specific platform; no architecture or sanitiser requirement is stated in the evidence, so the defect is assumed to reproduce on standard x86_64 Linux and was not confirmed on other architectures.
Tz-aware DatetimeArray._add_offset sentinel issue is explicitly out of scope and must not be counted toward the transition.

Python version was not stated, and no era ceiling exists for NumPy, so a NumPy release newer than the one used upstream at PR time could in principle change float-to-int cast behaviour; this is unverified.

oracle.reference_source: TimedeltaIndex path in pandas raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta with message 'Overflow in timedelta division'
oracle.why: The check is a discrete exception-or-not decision on whether the float64 quotient magnitude reaches 2**63, so the test asserts an exception rather than a numeric tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy ebd40365c94b, td / other returns array([9223372036854775807]) without raising, so pytest.raises(OutOfBoundsTimedelta) reports DID NOT RAISE and the test fails; the same happens for td // other.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the scalar path detects the quotient magnitude >= 2**63 in float64 and raises OutOfBoundsTimedelta with 'Overflow in timedelta division' for both / and //, satisfying both pytest.raises assertions in every parametrization.
